sources: recreation.gov public campsite search for 10098538 (per-site catalog)

values.note: $16 per single site per night; $5 per extra vehicle parked at the site over 30 minutes (or use the overflow lot).

fees.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/kootenai/recreation/dorr-skeels-campground ('Single Site: $16 per night ... 50% discount with US Golden Age/Access or Interagency Senior/Access Passes') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10098538/rates (First-come, First-served Season 2026-05-22 to 2026-09-30: WalkIn standard non-electric 16) + recreation.gov notice ('you will need to pay the $5 extra vehicle fee or move the vehicle to the overflow parking area'), read 2026-10-22

discounts.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/kootenai/recreation/dorr-skeels-campground ('50% discount with US Golden Age/Access or Interagency Senior/Access Passes'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Not on the reservation system; first come, first served, and saving sites is prohibited. 16-day stay limit (recreation.gov also caps a year at 48 nights).

booking.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10098538 ('The campground campsites are not currently on the reservation system'; notices '16 day stay limit', 'Non-reservable sites are first come-first serve. Saving sites is prohibited.'; rules maxConsecutiveStay 16) + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/kootenai/recreation/dorr-skeels-campground ('16 day stay limit on all National Forest System Lands'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: Managed (host, water, garbage, fees) May through September; the Forest Service says the campground 'is available all year to visitors. Access is dependent upon weather conditions.'

season.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/kootenai/recreation/dorr-skeels-campground (Operational Hours: 'The campground is managed from May through September, but is available all year to visitors. Access is dependent upon weather conditions.'), read 2026-10-22

values.note: 8 overnight sites including one host site (plus 2 day-use sites): 5 in a tent-only area and 2 RV sites near the swimming beach. recreation.gov: 'Most sites offer an average length of 30 feet.'

sites.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/kootenai/recreation/dorr-skeels-campground ('8 overnight campsites, including one host site ... 5 sites are in the tent camping only area. The 2 sites for RV's are located near the swimming beach') + https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10098538, read 2026-10-22

values.note: Drinking water during the peak season (recreation.gov and the FS description); the FS page's amenity block says 'Potable water is not available at this site', contradicting its own description.

facilities.source: https://www.recreation.gov/api/camps/campgrounds/10098538 ('Vault toilets, garbage service and drinking water are available during the peak season') + https://www.fs.usda.gov/r01/kootenai/recreation/dorr-skeels-campground ('Amenities include potable water, vault toilets'; Restrooms 'Vault toilet(s)'; Water 'Potable water is not available at this site.'), read 2026-10-22

hookups.source: recreation.gov public campsite search for 10098538 (all 8 overnight sites typed STANDARD NONELECTRIC, water hookup No), read 2026-10-22

note: Kootenai NF campground at the north end of Bull Lake, 13 mi south of Troy on Hwy 56, among mature pines. The 2 RV sites are near the swimming beach and the boat ramp with dock; the rest are a tent-only area and a host site. A security gate is closed 10 pm to 7 am by the camphost. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the FS page and recreation.gov: $16 (2026), not reservable / FCFS, 16-day limit, 8 overnight sites incl. host, vault toilets, drinking water, no hookups, senior/access 50% off. Added season (managed May-Sept, available all year). Not stated: max rig length (sites average ~30 ft). No FS alert names Dorr Skeels or Hwy 56. Note trimmed of restated values.
flags: Missing phone: Three Rivers Ranger District 406-295-4693 (recreation.gov facility record).
Only 2 of the 8 overnight sites are RV sites (5 tent-only, 1 host), per the FS page.

The FS page contradicts itself on drinking water ('Amenities include potable water' vs 'Potable water is not available at this site'); recreation.gov says drinking water is available in the peak season, so potable_water true was kept.
